## F02.auto-compaction — Automatic compaction

Definition: When and how history is summarized without a command. (lever class: other)
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Claude Code automatically compacts conversation history when you approach context limits, which preserves important code and decisions while freeing space. In the SDK, it summarizes older history, keeping recent exchanges and key decisions, and emits a system message with subtype compact_boundary. A PreCompact hook fires on a compaction request. | ev: E-claude-code-02218, E-claude-code-00195, E-claude-code-00339
- codex-cli [supported, verified] `model_auto_compact_token_limit` is the token threshold that triggers automatic history compaction (unset uses model defaults). A scope setting controls whether it counts the full active context (`total`, the default) or only growth after the carried compaction-window prefix (`body_after_prefix`). | ev: E-codex-cli-00568, E-codex-cli-00923, E-codex-cli-00569
- copilot-cli [partial, verified] Copilot CLI automatically compacts conversation history in the background, summarizing it while preserving essential information. Compaction starts at approximately 80% of the context window, leaving about a 20% buffer for tool calls; the starting point is dynamic when static context already uses roughly 75% or more of the limit. | limit: Thresholds disagree: E-copilot-cli-01661 says auto-compaction starts when the conversation approaches 95% of the token limit; E-copilot-cli-00166 and E-copilot-cli-00623 say approximately 80%. | ev: E-copilot-cli-00166, E-copilot-cli-00623, E-copilot-cli-01661, E-copilot-cli-00445
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] When a conversation approaches the limit, VS Code automatically compacts older parts into a summary. The setting github.copilot.chat.summarizeAgentConversationHistory.enabled (Experimental, default true) controls it; false turns automatic compaction off. A PreCompact hook's trigger value is auto when the conversation exceeds the prompt budget. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00363, E-copilot-vscode-00983, E-copilot-vscode-00592, E-copilot-vscode-02348
- cursor [supported, unverified] When the context window gets close to full, Cursor compresses older parts of the conversation into a summary to leave more room for new conversation. The preCompact hook is called before compaction and is observational: it cannot block or modify the compaction behavior. | ev: E-cursor-00061, E-cursor-00909
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] The core automatically compresses the conversation history before sending it to the model. - grok-build [supported, verified] Grok auto-compacts as the context window fills. `[session] auto_compact_threshold_percent` (`0–100`, default `85`) compacts when context usage reaches that percent. `PreCompact` and `PostCompact` events cover conversation compaction runs. ## F02.context-inclusion — Context inclusion controls

Definition: Mentions, attachments, ignore files and what enters the window.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] The context window accumulates the system prompt, tool definitions, conversation history, tool inputs and tool outputs. Tool search is on by default and defers SDK MCP tools: Claude sees each tool's name and loads its full schema on demand. A subagent's intermediate tool calls and results stay inside it; only its final message returns to the parent. | ev: E-claude-code-00190, E-claude-code-00321, E-claude-code-00816
- codex-cli [supported, verified] In the CLI, mention paths explicitly or attach files with `/mention` and `@` path autocomplete; the IDE extension automatically includes open files, and `/ide-context` turns shared IDE context on or off. `tool_output_token_limit` (example 12000) sets tokens stored per tool output. Codex stops adding files once the combined size reaches `project_doc_max_bytes` (32 KiB by default). | ev: E-codex-cli-02047, E-codex-cli-02074, E-codex-cli-00925, E-codex-cli-02431
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] @ followed by a relative file path adds that file's contents to the prompt as context. For Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise users, content exclusion policies at enterprise, organization and repository levels are respected and excluded files are not used as context. - copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Each time the agent sends a request, VS Code assembles a prompt from multiple sources. ## F02.persistent-memory — Persistent memory

Definition: Memory that survives sessions: files, notes or an auto-memory store.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Claude can persist learnings across sessions using auto memory: notes Claude writes for itself based on your corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the MEMORY.md index loads at the start of every session. /memory can enable or disable auto memory. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 disables it. | ev: E-claude-code-09433, E-claude-code-10565, E-claude-code-07275, E-claude-code-08020
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Memories let ChatGPT and Codex carry useful context from earlier work into future work. Enabling Memories is off by default. `/memories` turns memory injection or memory generation on or off without leaving the TUI; `memories = false` disables generating and using local memories across chats. | ev: E-codex-cli-03124, E-codex-cli-00586, E-codex-cli-01178, E-codex-cli-01416
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Copilot Memory builds a persistent understanding of your repository by storing memories: coding conventions, patterns, and preferences Copilot deduces as it works. It remembers facts about repositories and personal coding preferences. --enable-memory enables memory in prompt mode (disabled by default). The feature is in public preview and subject to change. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01669, E-copilot-cli-01857, E-copilot-cli-00965, E-copilot-cli-03150
- copilot-vscode [supported, verified] When the memory tool is available, an agent can store notes (preferences, lessons from previous tasks, codebase information) for later in the same session or in future sessions. ## F02.memory-scope-loading — Memory scope and loading

Definition: Where memory lives, who sees it, and when it is loaded.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Auto memory is stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/; all worktrees share one directory, and the first 200 lines or 25 KB of the MEMORY.md index load at the start of every session. CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files above the working directory load at launch; subdirectory files load on demand. By default, --add-dir directories do not load memory files. | ev: E-claude-code-09433, E-claude-code-11208, E-claude-code-07986
- codex-cli [supported, verified] The main memory files live under `~/.codex/memories/`. ChatGPT web uses ChatGPT memory; local Codex clients use a separate local store, and the IDE extension uses the connected Codex host's local memory store. A setting (default true) lets Codex skip injecting existing memories into future sessions. | ev: E-codex-cli-03136, E-codex-cli-00617, E-codex-cli-03125, E-codex-cli-03130
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] Repository-level facts are available to all users with Copilot Memory access to that repository; user-level preferences only to that user's interactions, across repositories. Once enabled, it is on for users by default, applies in any repository using a supported Copilot feature, and users can opt out. Only the root agent can store or vote on memories; subagents can read them. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01860, E-copilot-cli-01862, E-copilot-cli-03153, E-copilot-cli-01054
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] All memory scopes are stored locally. User memory (/memories/) persists across all workspaces and conversations; its first 200 lines load automatically into every session. Repository memory (/memories/repo/) is scoped to the current workspace and persists across conversations, but is not a shared project file.
